segment portfolio into long term plays & short term plays

for long term plays commit to buying over a range of prices & time intervals with intent of holding for minimum X amount of time with a max price invalidation to cut when you're wrong

protects downsides while protecting upside by forcing yourself to hold for extended period of time if stop loss is not hit

e.g. you believe pump bottom is close, you want to buy $100k worth, you buy $20k each week next 5 weeks and cut entire position if it trades beneath .0014 on a high timeframe close like the weekly, slam entire size into position if it closes above .0034, now your entry is averaged over finite amount of time and you're less worried about low tf price action because you're still building the position, but you also have levels where you want to be fully in or fully out

then you just move to cold storage wallet & revisit when your time interval or price target is hit, say 6 months or new all time highs at .009

$NBIS outlook is pretty insane yet again.

$582.3M revenue (+454% Y/Y, +46% Q/Q) off ~50% adjusted EBITDA margin (AI Cloud). $8.04B cash on hand. 

Reiterates financial guide (2026 revenue: $3.0–$3.4B
2026 EoY ARR: $7–$9B), I was hoping for a raise, but it's already massive growth. 

Not really about this quarter financials, but these signals:

- "We could sell our entire 2027 capacity on these terms today." massive visibility on demand
- "4 customer agreements averaging over $1B+ each in contract value"
- Around 70% of Q2 deals included customer prepayments
- Contracted power guidance was raised again, from more ~4+ GW to 5 GW. (this used to be a concern vs. $IREN debate, but Nebius power guidance keeps going through the roof). 
- Expects $9B+ of prepayments in 2026 and says it has $40B+ of commitments.
- annual contract value per MW keeps going brrr (>$40M/mw for Q3 short term capacity deals)  

Same bear story will always be there (eg. large $5.66B of capex with current GAAP net loss), but demand is extreme with massive visibility, with increasing AI Cloud adjusted EBITDA margins ( 24% -> 45% -> 50% progression)

We kinda got this read through from all your hyperscaler cloud earnings and $CRWV backlog yesterday, but glad it's showing up in Weebius's earnings.

If you think I understand Intel better than the average person who follows the stock, you’re wrong. But I do think I understand the setup.

There is an interesting psychological situation around $95. The recent offering was heavily oversubscribed at that level, which makes me think there should be serious demand if the stock gets back there. It doesn’t mean $95 can’t break, but I think it should provide some kind of floor.

I also understand the near-term catalysts, so I built a strategy around the entire situation using stock and options.

$INTC is now my largest position, via stock and mainly through options with various expiration dates and strikes to mitigate risk. I can make money if the stock stays around here, falls somewhat, or moves higher, as long as it doesn’t crash or spike 15% in one day.

We’ve seen this many times with assets that go through a period of mania (silver, gold, memory stocks). They spike, cool down, and then slowly start climbing again. I believe $INTC could follow a similar path.

I might be wrong, but that’s the setup I’m betting on.

I might publish my full $INTC position later today or next week and explain every part of it and why I structured it this way.

Eight months of silence. Time to explain why…
 
I stopped posting on X because everything had become too noisy, especially in crypto.
 
When everyone is financially incentivized to post, the signal-to-noise ratio inevitably collapses. Engagement farming takes over. And at times, especially when prices are falling and everything becomes PvP, sharing real ideas starts to feel less worthwhile.
 
Sometimes the best thing you can do is step away and simply observe for a while.
 
And that’s exactly what I did.
 
I made a choice to put all my effort and focus into the people who subscribed to our research.
 
At GMI and @RealVision, I kept publishing. In fact, leaving X for a bit allowed me to produce some of the best and most original macro work of my career.
 
Removing myself from the noise turned out to be one of the best things I could have done, because it gave me back something I had been missing: time to think.
 
There were personal reasons too…
 
My third daughter arrived, and there is nothing quite like having a newborn at home to put the rest of life into perspective.
 
I also turn 40 this year. A milestone birthday has a way of doing the same thing. It makes you stop, take stock, and look hard at what you want from the next chapter.

And the truth is, what I wanted from the past decade of my life is not what I want from the next one.
 
@RaoulGMI and I have spoken for years about the period beyond 2030: a time when entirely new ways of thinking, working, and living emerge. 
 
If we’re even half right about what lies ahead, then I know exactly what I want from the next decade…
 
Whatever I build next, I want control. Over the direction. Over the product. And most importantly, over my time.
 
Because time is the real currency of life.
 
The need to take control of mine has been circling in my mind for years. I have finally decided to act on it.
 
So here is the change…
 
I have decided to step away from GMI and @RealVision to build something of my own. 
 
I’ll be launching my own macro research platform.
 
I won’t oversell it before it’s ready. But I know this much: it will be the most ambitious and comprehensive macro and investment framework I have ever built, and I’m incredibly excited about it.
 
More on this in Q4.
 
Now for the part that means the most to me…
 
@RaoulGMI, thank you.
 
For the trust, the friendship, and the opportunity to spend the past several years working together. It has been an important chapter in my career, and one I will always look back on with fondness and gratitude.
 
To everyone at @RealVision and GMI who made the work possible, week after week and month after month, thank you.
 
And most of all, thank you to the community…
 
Your questions made my research sharper. Your challenges made me think harder. You engaged with the ideas at a level I have rarely seen anywhere else, and you reminded me constantly why this work is worth doing.
 
Of everything I accomplished over the past few years, nothing means more to me than the friendships I made along the way.
 
The next couple of months are for my family and for building what comes next.
 
But i’ll be around, sharing ideas and perspectives whenever I have something worth saying.
 
In the meantime, enjoy the rest of your summer everyone...
